key_insight: A simple atom-deletion strategy can extract local atomic environments from large simulations more effectively than more complex shape-and-envelope methods for preparing DFT training inputs.
engineering_relevance: This improves the practical workflow for active learning and on-the-fly training of machine-learning interatomic potentials by enabling smaller, DFT-compatible periodic cells from massive atomistic simulations.
method: Benchmarked multiple extraction techniques for cutting local regions out of bulk simulation boxes.
Compared methods for embedding extracted environments into periodic DFT-ready configurations.
Tested across diverse systems: amorphous SiO2, Ta with screw dislocations, and molten C.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a benchmark across several challenging material classes, and the deletions method performed best relative to alternative extraction approaches.
watch_item: Extraction quality may depend on how the local environment and periodic-boundary padding are chosen, so the method still needs careful use for different chemistries and defect types.
paper_title: Extracting Atomic Environments for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials
